title: My sister booked my wedding venue for herself
parts: My sister booked my wedding venue for the exact same day as my wedding. And she thought I would never find out. Let me explain. I had been planning my wedding for two years. Small vineyard outside the city, June fourteenth, sunset ceremony. My sister Claire knew every single detail, because I told her everything. We were close. Or at least I thought we were. Three weeks before the wedding, the vineyard calls me. The manager sounds nervous. She asks if I want to confirm the change of name on the booking. I ask her what change. She goes quiet. Then she tells me that a woman called last month, said she was me, said the wedding was off, and asked to transfer the date and the deposit to a new couple. The new couple's names? Claire and her boyfriend Mark. My own sister had cancelled my wedding, using my name, and moved herself into my date. I didn't scream. I didn't call her. I asked the manager one question. Has anyone told Claire that I found out? She said no. And that is when I came up with a plan.

So the manager, her name was Diane, was horrified. She told me the transfer had not been finalized yet, because the deposit was still in my name. I asked Diane to do me a favor. Leave everything exactly as it is. Let Claire believe it worked. Diane hesitated, then she smiled and said she had a sister too. That night Claire called me, sounding so sweet. She asked how the planning was going. I told her it was perfect. I even asked her to give a speech. She said she would be honored. Honored. Meanwhile I was quietly calling every guest on my list. My parents, my aunts, my cousins, my friends. I told them the truth, and I told them to say nothing. Not one of them did. Then Diane called me again. Claire had just been in to do a tasting for her own wedding. On my date. At my vineyard. She had picked the same menu I had picked. She even asked for the same flowers. Diane asked me what I wanted her to do. I told her to say yes to everything. Because I had found something out about Mark. Something Claire did not know.

Mark was not just Claire's boyfriend. Two years earlier, before he ever met my sister, Mark had dated my best friend Jenna. And he had left her with eleven thousand dollars of debt on a credit card in her name. Jenna had the receipts. She had the messages. She had everything. So here is what happened on June fourteenth. Claire showed up at the vineyard in a white dress, ready to marry Mark on the day she had stolen from me. And every single seat was filled. With my guests. My family. My friends. Jenna, right in the front row. Claire thought they had come for her. Then Diane walked up to the microphone and announced that the booking was, and always had been, in my name. And that today's ceremony would be mine. I walked down the aisle. My fiance was waiting. Claire just stood there. Then Jenna stood up and asked Mark, in front of everyone, when she would be getting her eleven thousand dollars back. Mark left before the vows. Claire left right after him. I got married at sunset, exactly as I had planned. My sister did not get my day. She just got the truth.
